question: A research team spends much of each week manually copying findings between four separate documents. Which two responses fit this situation best? Select two.
options: A) Treat the copying itself as the thing to redesign, rather than speeding it up as it stands.
B) Have Claude consolidate the four documents into one source the team then maintains together.
C) Add a fifth document in which Claude records what it copied into each of the other four weekly.
D) Have Claude do the copying between all four documents on the team's behalf every week.
E) Keep all four documents and ask Claude to double the speed at which each one is updated.
correct_answers: A) Treat the copying itself as the thing to redesign, rather than speeding it up as it stands.
B) Have Claude consolidate the four documents into one source the team then maintains together.
explanations: Correct. Duplicated copying is a symptom of process design, so this is the case where redesign beats augmentation.
Correct. Consolidating to a single maintained source removes the duplication instead of automating it.
Incorrect. A fifth document adds another artefact to maintain and makes the duplication problem worse than before.
Incorrect. Automating the copying preserves four diverging documents and simply performs the waste faster.
Incorrect. Speeding up a redundant step leaves the structural problem, and four sources still drift apart from each other.
